what: a stream's length was read from what the container states: NUT and FLV state no stream duration, so loudness.py said 'the output reports no duration' (verified: false) for a NUT whose read-back was clean, and loop.py read NUT's container duration, its last packet's pts (6.061 s for 6.0: verified: false); MPEG-TS states the sound's length from the last PES timestamp, several AAC frames before its end, so cut.py's stream copy into .ts, .m2ts or .mts read 1.259 s of sound for the 1.536 s its packets hold and stream_lengths said 0.363 s short (verified: false)
escaped: probe() took each stream's duration from ffprobe's header and the Matroska DURATION tag only; MPEG-TS's estimate came within the 0.25 s tolerance for the tools' full-length encodes (0.19 s short for 3 s), and no test cut a copy into MPEG-TS and compared the lengths with the packets, nor wrote a NUT with any tool
mechanism: probe._packet_ends() reads the packets of a NUT, FLV or MPEG-TS file's last 10 s (ffprobe -read_intervals, no decode) and probe() gives each stream its last packet's end less its start, and NUT/FLV the latest end less the file's start as the container's length; test_nut_flv_and_mpegts_stream_lengths_are_read_from_their_packets holds cut, loop, loudness and probe to every packet of the file, and CapabilityGuard reads each container's lengths through probe.py
size_reason: 33 of the net lines counted from main are this fix's (probe._packet_ends() and its use, 30; the .flv table entry, 3); the other 30 are #754's commit, cherry-picked onto this branch because the .flv entry is built on its table and _copies_reordered_video(). Once #754 is merged, this fix alone is 33 net lines
